title: Chrome/Chromium accessibility, performance and reliability regressions
scope: Publicly documented accessibility, performance/memory, platform reliability, printing/PDF/download and extension-regression issues, investigated on 2026-11-21. Reuses completed documentary research; includes proposed verification but no local browser reproductions.

evidencePolicy.observedFacts: Direct observations are the retrieved public metadata, descriptions, comments, duplicate relationships and linked change descriptions. They establish what the public records say, not browser behavior observed by this project.
evidencePolicy.upstreamClaims: Reproduction results, rollout announcements, causal explanations and telemetry assessments are attributed to upstream reporters, developers or testers. An upstream report is not a submission by this project.
evidencePolicy.hypotheses: Possible shared causes and verification recommendations remain hypotheses or proposed work. None of the recommendations below was executed in this lane.
evidencePolicy.confidenceMeaning: Confidence describes documentary support and attribution, not a probability that any current installation exhibits the defect.
evidencePolicy.statusMeaning: Tracker status, upstream test outcome, landed change, verified build and release deployment are distinct. Later anecdotes do not automatically reopen a closed tracker record.
evidencePolicy.dateMeaning: Issue publication dates are creation timestamps. Modification dates may include administrative activity. Retrieval dates are separate; ambiguous documentation date metadata is not used as an established publication date.

issues.title: Regression: Ctrl+Plus/Ctrl+Minus zoom no longer announces percentage to screen readers
steps: Reported workflow: open Chrome and any webpage, then enable a screen reader; the original Windows report names NVDA, JAWS and Narrator.
Press Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus repeatedly and compare the announced percentage with the actual new zoom value.
Distinguish no percentage announcement from the intermediate failure that announces the previous percentage.
issues.expected: The screen reader announces the new zoom percentage, such as 110% or 120%, after each keyboard zoom change.
issues.observed: Upstream reporters and testers heard menu labels such as Normal or Reset instead of the percentage. An intermediate fix could announce the previous zoom value. Later upstream tests reported the correct percentages on specific fixed builds; this project ran no browser test.
issues.regressionAssessment: Upstream testing reported cross-platform reproduction and a bisect boundary of 144.0.7546.0 good versus 144.0.7547.0 bad.

history.event: Initial changes disabled the zoom page-action migration parameter and updated the accessible name with the current percentage.
An earlier Fixed (Verified) state was reopened after reports that changing from X% to Y% announced X%. A test on 145.0.7632.67 was also clarified as a mini-branch build without the merged fix.
The follow-up updated zoom page-action properties before bubble visibility; backports and version-specific tests followed.
Final displayed transition to Fixed (Verified). The original Settings > Appearance workaround is historical rather than proof of the corrected keyboard path.

upstreamVerification.outcome: Upstream comments report the expected percentage announcements; the earlier verification preceded an additional stale-value fix.
Comment 35 reports successful verification and explicitly says the Extended Stable build was unavailable for Linux verification.

verificationStillNeeded: On a current supported build, compare the exact spoken/Braille value with the new zoom value for both increasing and decreasing zoom.
Test the keyboard path itself; the presence of speech or a working settings control is insufficient.
limitations: Historical upstream-fixed regression; no present-day local failure is established.
All testedVersions remain empty because verification was performed upstream, not by this project.
Linked change descriptions were read from issue history, not independently built or reviewed.

submission.reason: Existing upstream report reviewed as evidence; this project did not submit or modify it.

issues.title: Regression M153: Browser hangs on focus change with web accessibility enabled, many form controls slotted into display:none containers in shadow DOM
platforms: Windows 11 in an upstream negative test
reportedVersions: 153.0.8010.47 and later, according to the original report
steps: Reported fixture: reproducer.zip supplies a server for a parent page on localhost port 8000 and a cross-site iframe on 127.0.0.1.
Enable Web accessibility; the report also lists native accessibility API support, text metrics and extended properties.
In the fixture, select Tab1, focus an input outside the iframe, then select Tab0.
Retain many form controls with closed shadow roots, nested slots and display:none containers; the reporter varies hidden-control count to change failure frequency.
issues.expected: Focus moves normally between the cross-site iframe and top page without a browser-wide stall.
issues.observed: The reporter described all tabs and windows hanging for 15 to 60 seconds and stated that enabling web accessibility alone was sufficient. A tester initially could not reproduce; the reporter later reported successful operation on specific newer builds. No local reproduction was run.
issues.regressionAssessment: Reporter identified Chrome 152 as good and 153.0.8010.47 as affected. Exact applicability to other platforms or all later builds is not established.

quotations.text: Tested with 157.0.8101.39, where i can't reproduce it as well.

history.event: Reporter said Windows UI Automation can enable accessibility without a screen reader. Suppressing platform accessibility integration was described as a mitigation, but was explicitly unsuitable for screen-reader users.

An upstream tester did not observe a hang on Windows 11 with 155.0.8059.85. Written steps used port 9000 rather than the report's port 8000; equivalence of the test conditions is not established here.
A developer stated related issue 568011891 was fixed in 158.0.8122.0 and requested verification of this report. This was a proposed relationship, not a demonstrated duplicate.
After the reporter could not reproduce on 159.0.8130.0, the tracker moved to Fixed (Verified). The later 157.0.8101.39 result is retained exactly as reported, without inferring a release channel.

upstreamVerification.outcome: Reporter could not reproduce in comment 10; the verifier thanked the reporter and closed the issue.
Reporter also could not reproduce in comment 12.

relatedIssues.relationship: Developer-linked potentially relevant fix; full related record not read.
Reporter-linked possibly related issue, not a demonstrated duplicate; full record not read.
Commenter suggested the same problem; full record and shared cause not established.

verificationStillNeeded: Retain cross-site focus changes, hidden nested slots, high control counts and enabled accessibility when validating the target build.
Confirm inclusion of the relevant fix rather than assuming all higher-looking version strings or channels are equivalent.
Use accessible operation as the acceptance condition rather than turning accessibility off.
limitations: The fixture was not downloaded or executed; the scaling and stall-duration observations belong to the reporter.
The precise common cause with linked issues and the exact release/channel mapping of reported fixed builds were not established.

submission.reason: Existing upstream report and later verification were reviewed; no report was submitted by this project.

issues.title: Serious accessibility issues for screen reader users: narrowed Linux first-run/Orca report
steps: Reported workflow: start Orca, then launch Chrome/Chromium for the first time.
Inspect whether the initial banner is announced and can be operated, and whether a browser window actually launches.
The reporter said Space or Enter dismissed the banner; subsequent normal browsing was accessible. This workaround was not verified here.
issues.expected: First-run UI is announced and operable with Orca, allowing users to enter the browser without discovering an unannounced dismissal by chance.
issues.observed: The original reporter described complete screen-reader silence but then narrowed the failure to a first-run banner. Upstream testers could read normal pages and could not reproduce the reported failure. The latest substantive developer comment questioned whether the video instead showed a browser-launch problem.
issues.regressionAssessment: Reporter labels it a regression from version 153; upstream reproduction and the actual defective component remain unconfirmed.

quotations.text: When you start chromium/chrome for first time it appears a banner that Orca can't read. After this all is regularly usable and accessible.

history.event: Reporter narrowed the initial global-silence claim to the initial banner; normal browser operation reportedly worked afterward.
Upstream test on Debian with 154.0.8037.92 found that Orca read Chrome pages. This did not resolve the narrowed first-run question.
Developer said the supplied video did not show the browser launching and asked whether this was a launch issue rather than a screen-reader issue. Final metadata remains Assigned, not fixed or closed.

hypotheses.claim: The reporter guessed that the banner concerns license/conditions acceptance and that a GTK gtk-modules warning might be related.
hypotheses.assessment: Neither banner identity nor the warning's causal role was established.

verificationStillNeeded: Prioritize an isolated first-run Orca scenario, recording the initial UI's accessible role/name, focus and keyboard behavior.
Determine whether the browser actually launches before attributing silence to accessibility.
Do not present this report as a confirmed Chrome 154 browser-wide screen-reader outage.
limitations: Confirmed public report, but an upstream-unconfirmed runtime defect with no fix or duplicate relationship established.
Normal-page speech is not sufficient to validate the narrowed first-run scenario.
No local browser or screen-reader actions were performed.

issues.title: Large memory regression on Windows BETA/Stable
steps: No public minimal step-by-step reproduction was supplied by this telemetry-focused record.
The upstream investigation compared Windows Beta/Stable private memory footprint around the M142-to-M143 transition and investigated accessibility-related COM references.
A relevant public fixture or code-derived scenario is still needed before executing a meaningful local memory-soak test.
issues.expected: Accessibility-related COM references are eventually released and the relevant workload does not leak memory without bound.
issues.observed: Upstream reported a private-memory-footprint regression not visible in UMA heap-profiler metrics. A linked fix description identifies three AccessibleObjectFromWindow callers failing to release returned COM references. The developer closed the regression based on nonpublic UMA graphs after backports; no local memory measurements were taken.
issues.regressionAssessment: Upstream telemetry assessment points to the M142-to-M143 transition. This is not a claim that all Chrome workloads leak memory.

quotations.text: Three callers were failing to do so, leading to unbounded memory leaks.
quotations.attribution: Change description embedded in upstream comment 15

history.event: Developer identified issue 471578422 and change 7486667 as a suspected cause/fix, pending deployment assessment.
The M144 backport described retaining returned COM references in objects that eventually release them.

Closing comment says the change landed in 144.0.7559.114 and 145.0.7632.20 and the bug is fixed based on UMA graphs. Retrieved metadata is Fixed (Verified); the telemetry itself is not public evidence available to this lane.

upstreamVerification.outcome: Developer identified these as landed backport builds and assessed field improvement using nonpublic telemetry. This is not a locally reproduced pass or a public minimal-fixture result.

relatedIssues.relationship: Linked accessibility/COM leak report; full related record was not investigated here.

hypotheses.claim: The discussion also explored pending IndexedDB transactions.
hypotheses.assessment: Do not present that separate investigative observation as the proven cause of this accessibility-related regression.

verificationStillNeeded: Obtain a small relevant public reproduction or derive one from the actual code in a separately scoped engineering task.
For an accessibility/caret/focus soak, observe process private memory as well as managed or JavaScript heap; a heap-only check may miss the described allocation category.
limitations: No public, independently checkable memory-growth amount or tested acceptance threshold was established.
The fix mechanism and population-level improvement are upstream claims of different kinds; linked code was not built or locally tested.
Nonpublic telemetry and diagnostics were not accessed or included.

issues.title: All Chromium windows freeze during fullscreen/multi-monitor transitions
platforms: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti in the original report
reportedVersions: NVIDIA driver 596.49 and other tested driver versions
steps: Reported setup: a 2560x1440 240-Hz primary display and a 1920x1200 60-Hz secondary display.
Play a YouTube video on the primary display, enter fullscreen, then exit fullscreen; some reports say watching longer before exiting makes failure more likely.
Alternatively, keep the video on the primary display while detaching another tab and moving the new window to the secondary display.
Repeat sufficiently to observe the intermittent problem, distinguishing all-window visual updates, input responsiveness, audio and cursor behavior.
issues.expected: All windows remain responsive and continue rendering through fullscreen and cross-display transitions.
issues.observed: The original reporter described all windows in one browser instance stopping visual updates, with video freezing and audio sometimes continuing briefly. Large window resizing sometimes restored rendering. Upstream testers did not reproduce this freeze, but later acknowledged a related mixed-refresh-rate/independent-flip throttling defect.
issues.regressionAssessment: Reporter labels this a regression across multiple Chromium-based browsers and drivers. A specific introductory build or universal GPU/platform scope is not established.

quotations.text: Although I haven't been able to reproduce the freeze described, we have discovered a bug in the interaction between chrome, mixed refresh rate monitors and hardware iflip.

history.event: Upstream testing with a different GPU/display configuration did not reproduce. Reporter said disabling DirectComposition prevented the freeze on their system but was not an ideal long-term workaround.
A developer explicitly separated the NVIDIA whole-window freeze from AMD reports where the browser remained responsive but the cursor disappeared.
Even an upstream test on a 320-Hz monitor did not reproduce the original freeze.
Reporter said disabling MPO appeared to help but explicitly had not used that configuration long enough to be certain.
Developer acknowledged related video/rendering throttling and hoped its fix would also resolve the original freeze. Linked changes are not evidence of a shipped or verified freeze fix.

hypotheses.claim: DirectComposition/hardware independent-flip involvement has supporting reporter experiments.
hypotheses.assessment: The original freeze's root cause and responsibility across Chromium, Windows/DWM and GPU drivers remain unresolved; the related throttling defect is not proof of identity.

verificationStillNeeded: Use a high-refresh multi-monitor Windows scenario, including longer video viewing before transitions and enough attempts for an intermittent failure.
Track paint, input, audio and cursor separately; preserve the distinction between a frozen browser and an invisible cursor.
Validate any candidate fix on the original symptom before treating the related throttling change as a solution.
limitations: Original freeze remains upstream-unconfirmed despite a public report and related engineering finding.
DirectComposition/MPO workarounds are reporter observations, not validated general recommendations.
No local GPU/display testing, flag changes or registry changes occurred.

submission.reason: Existing public upstream report reviewed; no project submission or local reproduction.

issues.title: Printing only an iframe as PDF shows incorrect title as file name
steps: Reported sample: https://jsfiddle.net/6jt3kzgw/ creates an iframe whose srcdoc document has a title distinct from the parent page.
Focus the iframe and invoke iframe.contentWindow.print().
Choose Save as PDF and compare the suggested filename with the iframe and parent titles.
Inspect the print-preview header separately, because it may already use the correct frame title.
issues.expected: When printing a titled iframe, the suggested PDF filename uses that iframe's title; the report proposes falling back to the parent title when no frame title is present.
issues.observed:
Upstream reproduction found that the parent/tab title becomes the suggested PDF filename even when the print-preview header has the iframe's correct title. A later reporter still saw the behavior in Chrome 144.0.7559.109. November's update request is not a new current-build reproduction.

issues.title: DevTools is blocked by policy unexpectedly - main bug
steps: Reported PDF scenario: use a managed test configuration where DeveloperToolsAvailability is unset/default or 0.
Open a simple HTML page containing an iframe pointing to an actual PDF, then attempt to inspect the main page.
A separate scenario in the discussion uses an enterprise-installed extension injecting its iframe into a normal webpage; attempt host-page inspection there too.
Keep host-page inspection distinct from direct inspection of a policy-restricted extension.
issues.expected: Host-page DevTools availability follows the intended managed policy without unintended whole-tab blocking solely because the page embeds a component PDF viewer or an affected extension frame.
issues.observed:
Upstream users and testers saw an organization-blocked DevTools message on otherwise ordinary pages containing PDFs or managed-extension frames. An initial PDF exception, subsequent rollback and incomplete rollback behavior led to further fixes. Later upstream PDF-scenario verification passed on 152.0.7977.64.

issues.title: Drag/input freeze: current window freeze and no mouse/keyboard action allowed
reportedVersions: 148.0.7778.96 (first defect after a backport, according to upstream bisect discussion)
steps: Reported reproduction A: use test-page.html attached at canonical comment 14 and repeatedly drag its red square into a neighboring text editor. The reporter estimated roughly 20 to 80 repetitions, sometimes fewer with faster dragging.
After the failure, use the browser toolbar to refresh and attempt another drag; record whether mouse/keyboard delivery stops even while rendering or scrolling continues.

Reported reproduction B: rapidly click and drag the draggable buttons/cells in the fixture at canonical comment 38; observe pairing of dragstart and dragend and whether elements become permanently undraggable.
The consolidated duplicate also uses https://sortablejs.github.io/Sortable/ with repeated dragging, refreshing and another attempt to interact.
issues.expected: Aborted or failed drag initialization clears browser drag state and delivers the necessary dragend cleanup, preserving mouse/keyboard input and application interaction.
issues.observed:
Upstream first found whole-tab input suppression after repeated drag initialization failures. A first fix addressed that repro, but a second regression could omit dragend and strand application state while rendering remained alive. Both repros later passed upstream tests. Later Salesforce/general freeze reports were explicitly discussed as potentially unrelated rather than silently reopening the two fixed drag defects.
